title: Shortest Bridge
summary: Given an n x n binary matrix where 1 represents land and 0 represents water, and knowing there are exactly two separate islands of land (1's), determine the minimum number of water cells (0's) that need to be changed to land in order to connect the two islands into a single island.
statement: Given an n x n binary matrix where 1 represents land and 0 represents water, and knowing there are exactly two separate islands of land (1's), determine the minimum number of water cells (0's) that need to be changed to land in order to connect the two islands into a single island.
constraints: grid is square and contains exactly two four-connected islands.
Changing one water cell to land costs one.
Return the minimum changes needed to connect the islands.
hints: Mark every cell of one island first.
Run a multi-source BFS outward through water from that entire island.
The first cell of the other island is reached after the minimum number of water layers.
BFS layers represent exactly the number of converted water cells on the shortest bridge.
editorial: BFS layers represent exactly the number of converted water cells on the shortest bridge.

tests.explanation: Either single separating water cell connects the diagonal islands.
The closest land cells have Manhattan distance three, requiring two water changes.
